title: Is there a general criterion for when Gal(X^n - a/ℚ) is dihedral

problemStatement.formal: For $a \in \mathbb{Q}^{\times}$ and $n \ge 1$, determine a decidable criterion (in terms of $n$ and the prime factorization of $a$) for $\operatorname{Gal}(X^n - a/\mathbb{Q}) \cong D_m$ for some $m \ge 2$.
problemStatement.plain: Find a decidable criterion characterising when the Galois group of X^n − a over ℚ is dihedral.
whyMatters: Generalises the parent gallery entry's D_4 realization (n=4, a=2) to a uniform criterion across all (n, a).
Connects three Mathlib gaps: Capelli's irreducibility theorem, generic metacyclic order |G| = n·φ(n), and explicit dihedral identification.
Provides a concrete decidable predicate suitable for a future `def`/`theorem` scaffold.

proven: Capelli's theorem (1897): X^n - a reducible iff (∃ prime p | n: a ∈ (ℚ*)^p) or (4 | n and a ∈ -4(ℚ*)^4).
Velez (1979): G_n(a) = ℤ/n ⋊ (ℤ/n)* (the full metacyclic group of order n·φ(n)) generically when X^n - a is irreducible and √[n]a ∉ ℚ(ζ_n).
Schinzel–Velez classification: dihedral case reduces to (n, a) such that the cyclotomic action collapses to {±1} ⊂ (ℤ/n)*.
Parent gallery: |Gal(X^4 - 2 / ℚ)| = 8 ≅ D_4 (27 theorems, 0 sorries, ℝ-embedding proof).
open: Lean formalization of Capelli's full theorem (only prime-n case partially in Mathlib).
Decidable Lean predicate isDihedralCriterion(n, a) tying to DihedralGroup m via MulEquiv.
Proof of equivalence between the criterion and the abstract Galois group identification.

insights: Every G_n(a) embeds into the metacyclic semidirect product M_n = ℤ/n ⋊ (ℤ/n)* — dihedral is necessarily a subgroup of M_n.
For odd n, dihedral D_n requires the cyclotomic action on ℤ/n to collapse to {±1} — a sporadic condition rarely satisfied for rational a.
For n = 2k with k odd, dihedral D_(2k) requires φ(k) = 2, i.e., k ∈ {3, 4, 6}, giving n ∈ {6, 8, 12}.
n = 4 is the canonical dihedral case: (ℤ/4)* = {±1} has order 2 = φ(4), so generic |G| = 8 = |D_4|.
The parent gallery's ℝ-embedding argument (a > 0) does not generalize to a < 0; a uniform criterion needs Capelli-based reasoning.
mathlibGaps: Capelli's full theorem (4 | n and -4b^4 exception): ~200 lines of new infrastructure.

Kappe–Warren discriminant-based dihedral test for n=4 (low-hanging fruit, ~50 lines).
